title: Installing Arduino Core and ESP-IDF

spans.text: Goal: apply “Installing Arduino Core and ESP-IDF” to a real program or device. The key principle is: ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building. In a project, follow this guidance: Start with the official `hello_world` example and record the working toolchain version.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

spans.code:
idf.py --version
idf.py set-target esp32
idf.py build
idf.py -p PORT flash monitor

spans.text: Flash and monitor output depends on a connected board, selected serial port, target, and firmware.

Arduino-ESP32 offers the familiar sketch model. ESP-IDF is Espressif's component-based CMake/Kconfig and FreeRTOS framework; choose for project needs and pin the version.

`idf.py` commands are specific to an ESP-IDF project and toolchain. Arduino-ESP32 uses its own Arduino CLI/IDE board package and build workflow; these commands are not Arduino sketch commands.

On Windows, macOS, and Linux, use Espressif's official ESP-IDF Installation Manager or the current installation path in the ESP-IDF documentation. The manager can install compatible Python, Git, CMake, Ninja, compiler, and debug tools. Open the ESP-IDF terminal after setup, select the exact ESP32 target, build an official example, and flash the board's USB port. Arduino-ESP32 Core is installed as an Arduino IDE board package and is a different workflow from ESP-IDF.

Key line: `idf.py --version`
What it does: ESP-IDF selects the chip target before building.
Why it is used: Start with the official `hello_world` example and record the working toolchain version.
If omitted or changed: Linux may need distribution-specific serial-device permissions; apply only the permission steps in Espressif's official instructions.

spans.text: Obtain the installer only from Espressif; a wrong chip target or port causes flashing failures.
